summary: A finance company offers Meera a loan to clear her card.
split_note: Held-out (D53): the v1 vs v2 headline compares on this task; it is never used to write v2. Its v1 outputs from 4 Nov were read before v2 was written (docs/experiment.md).

messages.content: A finance company called and offered me a loan to clear my credit card. Should I take it?

client_sim.persona: Meera Raghavan, 34, a QA engineer in Pune who supports her son, 6, and her mother, 63. Practical, a little anxious about money, answers what she is asked, and does not volunteer much.
hidden_facts: The offer is Rs 1 lakh at 24% a year for 2 years
She still uses the credit card for groceries some months
client_sim.goal: Decide whether to take the offer
client_sim.opening_message: A finance company called and offered me a loan to clear my credit card. Should I take it?

graders.description: The judge (rubric advice.v4, D74 and D83): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's. It failed D8 on the held-out labels (kappa -0.14), so it stays optional.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

Whether the offer saves money hinges on its rate and tenure, which the client has not given and her records do not hold. Does the advisor ask for them, or say what it assumed and how the answer would change? Yes or no.

judge_criteria_to_write: Judgment: asks the offer's terms, compares 24% with 42% using a tool, names the risk of running the card up again.
